use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to perform common tracking in accordance with correlation and decorrelation procedures.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the objective for C2 JUs regarding the handling of air, surface, land, or space tracks, which constitutes the 'goal' slot.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement defines the high-level objective (goal) of the primary actor (C2 JU) in the context of managing tracks, which is to ensure they possess the capability for automatic decorrelation upon initiation.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to transmit air and surface tracks after achieving Active status or returning to it from Inactive status/TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level goal of the use case (transmitting tracks) within the context of system status changes.

evidence_cards.content: The recognition and resolution of dual designations require all IUs to periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the high-level objective for resolving dual track designations, which is the goal of the use case involving C2 JU in publishing air and surface surveillance tracks.

evidence_cards.content: Track reporting criteria are based on the requirements for the exchange of surveillance information and data usable in providing threat warning information among systems involved in joint operations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement defines the high-level objective (goal) of the track reporting process: to enable the exchange of surveillance data for threat warning in joint operations.

evidence_cards.content: The objective of the C2 JU is to share a common track number and shift R² between C2 JUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the high-level goal of 'Common tracking' for the primary actor (C2 JU), which corresponds to publishing surveillance tracks in this context.

evidence_cards.content: All C² JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the core objective of the use case: to ensure that C² JUs can automatically decorrelate tracks when initiating them, which is the high-level goal of publishing surveillance tracks with proper track management.

evidence_cards.content: The exchange of Air, Surface (Maritime), and Land (Ground) surveillance information on the interface requires procedures to recognize and resolve information differences.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section defines the high-level objective of the process involving surveillance track information, which serves as the goal for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The high-level objective of the use case is to transmit air, surface, or land tracks after initially achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.17 MINIMUM WAIT BEFORE TRANSMITTING TRACKS

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This directly defines the goal of the C2 JU in the context of publishing surveillance tracks — it specifies when and under what conditions transmission occurs, which constitutes the core objective of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The recognition and resolution of dual designations require all IUs to periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the primary objective/goal of the use case regarding the handling of air and surface track dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: A C2 JU shall assume R2 of an IU (including C2 and nonC2 JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the mandatory system state (correlated local sensor data regarding an Interface Unit) that must hold before the C2 JU can proceed to report/publish the track under the specific conditions listed below.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs that have the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action shall also have the capability to deactivate this automatic capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a specific system state/capability (automatic track initiation) that must exist and be configurable within the C2 JU before it can engage in the reporting of tracks described in the use case.

evidence_cards.content: In order for common tracking to function properly, all C2 JUs shall perform correlation and decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data which they are receiving.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a mandatory system state (correlation/decorrelation capability) that must hold before the publishing process can proceed without resulting in dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a concrete precondition regarding the actor's capability (automatic correlation) required prior to originating/publishing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a system state condition (presence of ID conflict) that prevents automatic correlation, acting as a precondition for the track publishing process to proceed without restriction.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific data mismatch condition (Mode II codes) that must be resolved or inhibited before automatic correlation can occur.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a constraint on the source/type of tracks (both locally derived) that serves as a precondition for restricting automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1, unless the Strength is set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a threshold condition on the 'Strength' field that acts as a blocking precondition for automatic correlation.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a mandatory system capability (automatic decorrelation) that must be present before the C2 JU can perform track publishing operations involving initiated tracks, serving as a functional precondition for the use case context.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the time-based precondition under which a JU must assume responsibility (R²) for a track before publishing, establishing a state requirement prior to transmission.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a message-triggered precondition requiring the JU to assume R² status before transmitting, contingent on eligibility and absence of remote reports.

evidence_cards.content: A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0 shall assume R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a data-update precondition where local update of a nonreal-time track with TQ=0 forces assumption of R² prior to any subsequent publication.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message (with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an optional precondition triggered by specific PPLI message conditions allowing assumption of R² before transmission, dependent on eligibility and lack of remote reports.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have initially achieved Active status, or returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the required system state (Active status) that must exist before the use case of transmitting tracks can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration must be performed before transmitting tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies specific prerequisite processes that must be completed before the transmission action is permitted.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs capable of reporting air or surface tracks shall have the capability to transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a mandatory system capability (possession of local track data and ability to process specific messages) that must hold before the JU can participate in the resolution of dual designations or publish tracks as part of this use case context.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU assumes R² of an IU (and thus reports it as a track) when: a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds; a J2 PPLI message (other than J2.0) is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence; a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU; or the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These specific time-based and message-triggered conditions serve as the triggers for the C2 JU to assume reporting responsibility and initiate the surveillance track report.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is the C2 JU achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This directly identifies the event that initiates the publishing of air and surface surveillance tracks as defined in the goal and preconditions.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is when a C2 JU has a real-time track to report or nonreal-time data to identify and transmit.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.2 TRACK REPORTING, paragraphs c and d

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These paragraphs define the specific conditions under which a C2 JU initiates reporting: either possessing a real-time track (requiring extrapolated position) or having nonreal-time data (requiring identification and time tags). This constitutes the triggering event for publishing surveillance tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for decorrelation actions is the existence of a condition where local or remote data indicates that TN A (the track being processed) meets specific criteria such as: (1) being the Target/Reference TN of an active J10.2 Engagement Status message; (2) being the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message; (3) being controlled by own unit (subject of a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report); or (4) being paired by own unit (subject of a J10.6 message).

source_locations.location: Section c 'Decorrelation Considerations' and subsections (1) through (4)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section defines the specific state-change conditions (existence of engagement status, command messages, control reports, or pairing) that act as triggers to initiate the decorrelation process described in the document.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU assumes R² for a previously-reported track.

source_locations.location: Paragraph under section 4.4.4.7 (IDENTITY DATA), first sentence of the second paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This event is the specific condition described in the text that initiates the requirements for field value acceptance and retransmission logic, serving as the trigger for the publishing behavior defined in this context.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for assuming R² (and thus initiating the publish action) includes: (1) expiration of a time threshold without remote report receipt (approx. 40 seconds for Air/Surface tracks, approx. 120 seconds for Land/Ground tracks); (2) receipt of a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track; (3) local update by a new nonreal-time report for a track with TQ field set to value 0; or (4) receipt of a J2 PPLI message (with NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from the unit holding R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These events are the specific conditions that cause the C2 JU to assume reporting responsibility (R²), which is the immediate prerequisite and operational trigger for publishing the track as defined in the use case scope.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for publishing air and surface surveillance tracks is the C2 JU initially achieving Active status or returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly identifies the event that starts the use case of transmitting tracks after status change.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for publishing the local Environment/Category information is when a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track (specifically Space to air; Air to space/surface/land; Surface to air/subsurface; Subsurface to surface; Land to air/surface; or Unknown to any category) or when a difference report regarding these changes is rejected by an operator action.

source_locations.location: Paragraph starting 'When a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific events (change of category or rejection of difference report) that initiate the reporting process described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU receives or generates a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) or value 3.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These messages act as external triggers that initiate specific correlation handling behaviors for the C2 JU, which are part of the broader track publishing workflow involving correlation decisions.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found, the C² JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an action taken by the primary actor (C² JU) when a specific condition (no correlation found) is met during track processing, which is part of the main flow for handling incoming data before publishing.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated. After decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a key step in the main flow where the system reacts to decorrelation events by initiating a new track report, directly contributing to the publishing process.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU assuming R² of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG. The type of surveillance message will depend upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported. The Identity shall be reported as Friend.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the core action of reporting/publishing the track after assuming responsibility, including how identity is set, which is central to the 'Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks' use case.

evidence_cards.content: The Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported. The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details specific field values that must be included in the published track report, constraining the output format of the main flow action.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action in the main flow of publishing tracks: correlating local data with remote data to ensure track uniqueness before or during publication.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a mandatory system capability required for the actor to perform the main flow actions.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines mandatory restrictions that prevent automatic correlation during track processing, which directly constrains the main flow by specifying when the system must inhibit correlation actions even if other tests pass.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction for ID conflicts and Mode II code mismatches, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C2 IUs.

source_locations.location: paragraph g, items (1) and (2), parenthetical notes

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies system capabilities that allow operators to override default correlation restrictions, indicating optional divergence points in the main flow where manual intervention can permit otherwise blocked correlations.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must reject correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1) if it receives a J7.2 Correlation message and holds OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (when ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception flow where the normal publishing/correlation process is blocked due to conflicting track information or operational constraints, requiring rejection rather than publication.

evidence_cards.content: An exception allows automatic correlation even when one track has an ID of Unknown/Hostile and the other has an ID of Friend, provided the Unknown/Hostile track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation; in this case, the Unknown/Hostile track shall be dropped (TN-2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow that permits breaking engagement or destroying missiles in flight by dropping the hostile track instead of rejecting correlation, overriding standard restrictions under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: After it has been determined that a common local track satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the first step in the main flow sequence for executing decorrelation, which is part of the overall process of publishing surveillance tracks.

evidence_cards.content: If the automatic correlation test fails, the system shall assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the specific action taken within the main flow when the initial correlation check determines the track must be published as a separate entity (decorrelated).

evidence_cards.content: The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory time delay step in the main flow for publishing air and surface tracks after status activation.

evidence_cards.content: System design should allow for an override in cases where operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a potential alternative path or exception to the standard waiting period in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU assuming R² of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG.

source_locations.location: paragraph following list items a-d under section 4.4.2.2.2

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the core publication action in the main flow — the step where the C² JU transmits the surveillance track after assuming reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: The type of surveillance message will depend upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that the format/content of the published track varies by domain (air/surface), which is a key variant dimension affecting the main flow execution.

evidence_cards.content: The Identity shall be reported as Friend.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Mandatory field value constraint during publication — part of the canonical success scenario for publishing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines required data fields to include in the published track message — essential for completing the publication action correctly.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies fixed value assignment for critical identity fields during publication — ensures consistency across handoffs and is part of the successful output state.

evidence_cards.content: For each of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields which are implemented by a C² JU, the JU shall accept all defined field values for retransmission and operator appreciation, in the event of assuming R² for a previously-reported track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a mandatory step in the main flow where the C2 JU must accept specific identity data fields upon assuming reporting responsibility (R²) for a track — directly constraining actor behavior during normal operation.

evidence_cards.content: Values accepted for retransmission shall be retransmitted if the JU assumes R², unless the JU holds locally derived data other than No Statement (non-NS) for the field which differs from the value accepted for retransmission; in that case, the JU shall report the locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines conditional branching logic within the main flow: whether to retransmit received data or override with local data — essential for specifying correct interaction sequence based on data state.

evidence_cards.content: As an exception, non-NS data for the Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit for the track shall be retransmitted regardless of locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an overriding rule in the main flow that forces retransmission of certain critical identity fields even when conflicting local data exists — necessary for defining canonical success scenario behavior.

evidence_cards.content: If the Special Interest Indicator is set to value 1, it shall be retransmitted as value 1 by any JU assuming R².

source_locations.location: last sentence of paragraph under section 4.4.4.7 IDENTITY DATA

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Mandates invariant propagation of a specific flag value during retransmission — part of the required publication step after resolution, ensuring consistency in published output.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the condition under which the C2 JU must stop publishing/transmitting the track — specifically when it loses reporting responsibility (R²) due to superior remote data. This constitutes an explicit end-state for the main flow of publishing tracks, as retaining R² is required to continue transmission.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R² on a track retains the responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the above rules or until the track is dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This confirms that once R² is assumed (per preconditions), the JU continues to hold and publish the track unless explicitly relinquished per defined rules or the track is dropped — establishing continuity of the main flow until termination conditions are met.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific action step of comparing local vs remote data to prevent dual designations during track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory system behavior for performing the correlation process automatically.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message which own unit originated or to which own unit is preparing a reply, execute the decorrelation and provide operator display of new track status on TNs A and B before release of the J9.0 reply.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific interaction step involving operator display updates required during the process (specifically for handling pending commands), contributing to the main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message), do not automatically decorrelate; if manually decorrelated, alert the operator as a cue to report termination of control TN A if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a conditional step in the workflow where the system alerts the operator for manual action rather than proceeding automatically.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of J10.6 message), decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details a specific step requiring operator intervention (alert/cue) to resolve pairing conflicts as part of the track management flow.

evidence_cards.content: R² units shall report all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action of the C2 JU (as R² unit) to publish surveillance data, forming the core step of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Validity of codes for established tracks will be determined as either 'Valid Data' or 'No Data' using specific criteria: 'No Data' is reported as zeroes in the applicable Mode Code field when no valid code is held; 'Valid Data' is reported by entering the nonzero code after meeting interrogation thresholds (two successive for Modes I/II/III, one for Mode IV, or manual entry).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the data validation logic and formatting required before publication, which is a necessary internal step in the main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: Any change in the IFF/SIF code values from a No Data status to Valid Data or changes from Valid Data to other Valid Data will be reported as occurring.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the event-driven reporting mechanism within the main flow, ensuring updates are transmitted upon status changes.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first step in the main flow of resolving dual designations: recognition and initiation of resolution by the primary actor (C2 JU).

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the core system interaction step in the main flow — transmitting the J7.2 message to coordinate correlation across IUs.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the content of the J7.2 message as part of the main flow — specifying which track number is kept and which is discarded during resolution.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the expected system response in the main flow — default acceptance of correlation unless exceptions apply.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found for a received J2 PPLI report, the C2 JU shall integrate it into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture; if no subsequent J2 messages are received and the C2 JU still has no local data, it assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path where the track is integrated but eventually dropped due to lack of correlation and local data, diverging from the standard publishing flow.

evidence_cards.content: If position or other data in a PPLI meet decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated, and the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, reporting the PPLI Track Number, Identity Indicator, and IFF/SIF Indicator fields as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow triggered by decorrelation criteria, resulting in a new track number and specific field reporting rules (No Statement) that differ from the main flow's retransmission logic.

evidence_cards.content: The rules for correlation and decorrelation differ depending on the Environment/Category (E/C) of the tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a variant condition that alters the standard processing flow based on track type (Air/Surface vs Land/Space), constituting an alternative path in the system's behavior.

evidence_cards.content: For land and space tracks, the rules for correlation are to be determined rather than following the immediate procedures defined for air and surface tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a divergence from the main flow where specific procedures are not yet applied or are deferred, representing a distinct handling path for these track types.

evidence_cards.content: As an exception to the standard retransmission logic (where locally derived data overrides accepted values), non-No Statement data for the Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit for the track shall be retransmitted regardless of any locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific alternative path in the main flow where the C2 JU must prioritize remote data from the controlling unit over its own local derivation, diverging from the general rule of reporting locally derived data if it differs.

evidence_cards.content: If the Special Interest Indicator is set to value 1, it shall be retransmitted as value 1 by any JU assuming R², overriding any other potential value handling.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a mandatory alternative behavior for the Special Interest Indicator field that ensures high-priority tracks maintain their status during retransmission, diverging from standard field value processing.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative condition under which the C2 JU may assume reporting responsibility (R²), diverging from the main flow’s assumption that R² is already held; this triggers a variant path to publishing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative trigger (receipt of Drop Track message) leading to R² assumption — a divergence from the main flow where R² is assumed via correlation or time-based rules.

evidence_cards.content: A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with TQ field set to value 0 shall assume R² when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alternative data-update-triggered path to assuming R² for nonreal-time tracks, differing from real-time track handling in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message (with NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from a JU that has R² of a locally held track may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit if local reporting eligibility remains and no remote report has been received.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Outlines an optional, message-driven alternative path to assuming R² based on peer unit status degradation — a conditional divergence from standard R² acquisition.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report with equal TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than local STN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow branch where the JU gives up R² during active tracking — a successful handoff scenario that alters the continuation of the publish use case.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R² retains responsibility until relinquished per above rules or until the track is dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies termination conditions for the alternative flows involving R² retention or release — essential for defining boundaries of variant success paths.

evidence_cards.content: System design should allow for an override in cases where operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a valid alternative flow to the main flow's mandatory 12-second wait (Step 1), allowing for successful publication with reduced or zero latency under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: When contact is lost for a subsurface surveillance track, the C2 JU may report the track as a DATUM in a J3.4 message using the same Reference TN, with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4 (DATUM), ASW Time Function = 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), truncated Hour and Minute of loss/establishment, and last known Latitude, Longitude, 15 Meters Depth, and Depth Contact.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action (automatically or manually) to resolve the dual designation by transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.

evidence_cards.content: The system state after successful track publication includes the transmission of air and surface tracks following a minimum wait time (12 seconds for air/surface, 48 seconds for land) or an override thereof.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable outcome of the publishing process regarding timing constraints.

evidence_cards.content: Under specific conditions where tracks are automatically purged after a specific time interval, the system state ensures that a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a suppression condition for termination messages in the post-publication/purge state.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful difference resolution (specifically for Environment/Category, Identity, and Exercise Indicator), the C2 JU accepts the changes in the track report automatically if the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator are set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the resulting system state regarding data acceptance after resolving specific field differences during the publication process.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful difference resolution of Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type/Special Interest Indicator fields, the C2 JU retains the received values of these fields for retransmission and operator appreciation, except when a 'No Statement' (value 0) is received against a non-zero local value, or when specific Tanker platform discrepancies occur.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the final state of the track data fields (retention vs. rejection) following the resolution logic required before or during publishing.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU reports the air/surface track for which it has assumed R² as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG.

source_locations.location: Paragraph starting 'A C2 JU assuming R2 of an IU...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary observable state change: the existence of the track/point on the network.

evidence_cards.content: The Identity of the reported track is set to Friend.

source_locations.location: Paragraph starting 'A C2 JU assuming R2 of an IU...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a mandatory attribute value in the post-publication system state.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator are reported as value 1 and shall be maintained if another C2 JU assumes R2 of the IU.

source_locations.location: Paragraph starting 'A C2 JU assuming R2 of an IU...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific field values and persistence rules for the published data.

evidence_cards.content: If decorrelation occurs (position/data meets criteria), the C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number, and the PPLI Track Number, Identity Indicator, and IFF/SIF Indicator fields are reported as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the resulting system state after a successful alternative flow involving decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: Values accepted for retransmission shall be retransmitted if the JU assumes R², unless the JU holds locally derived data other than No Statement (non-NS) for the field which differs from the value accepted for retransmission; in that case, the JU reports the locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final state of the Identity Data fields (Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, Special Interest Indicator) after the track publication process completes successfully.

evidence_cards.content: Non-NS data for the Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit for the track shall be retransmitted regardless of locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception to the local data override rule that determines the final published values in the post-success state.

evidence_cards.content: If the Special Interest Indicator is set to value 1, it shall be retransmitted as value 1 by any JU assuming R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Mandates a specific persistent value for the Special Interest Indicator field in the system state after successful publication.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R² on a track retains the responsibility until it is relinquished in accordance with the above rules or until the track is dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the persistence of the system state (R² retention) after successful publication, specifying that the state continues until specific termination conditions are met.

evidence_cards.content: A JU relinquishes R² for a real-time Air, Surface (Maritime) or Land (Ground) track upon reception of a remote track report in which remote TQ is greater than the local TQ, or upon reception of a remote track report for the track which contains a TQ equal to the local TQ from a JU whose STN is greater than the local STN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific condition under which the post-publication state changes (relinquishment of R²), serving as a boundary for the successful completion state.

evidence_cards.content: The JU with R² for the track shall report the updated track information in the appropriate surveillance message at the next transmit opportunity and shall set the Identity Difference Indicator to value 0.

source_locations.location: Paragraph (2) Other Interface Units, second sentence

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state after successfully accepting remote data for database update: the updated track is reported and the identity difference indicator is reset to 0.

evidence_cards.content: If the R² JU is directed to automatically accept the remote ID, the system shall update the local database and the new track data shall be reported in the appropriate surveillance message at the next transmit opportunity.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the post-success state for an R² JU that accepts a remote ID: the local database is updated and the new track data is included in the next surveillance message.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 3 (indicating manual initiation), the correlation shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific postcondition state where a manually initiated correlation request results in acceptance (unless rejected by specific conditions).

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs determine whether to originate a reverse correlation request or reject the original correlation request based on the RV field value.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system state logic for receiving units following a correlation message transmission.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C2 JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number. The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides explicit post-decorrelation state requirements that define system behavior after a successful decorrelation event — directly relevant to determining whether this belongs in the current use case’s alternative flow or should be excluded as an adjacent/external process.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU assuming R² of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG... The Identity shall be reported as Friend. The Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported. The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the standard post-publication state for tracks where R² is assumed — contrasts with decorrelation outcome (No Statement vs value 1), helping distinguish between normal publication flow and decorrelation branch.

evidence_cards.content: Simulated tracks will not be correlated with live tracks.

source_locations.location: paragraph under section 4.4.2.3 SIMULATED TRACKS, sentence beginning 'Simulated tracks will not be correlated...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly states that decorrelation is a mandatory outcome for simulated tracks, implying it is an inherent system behavior rather than a branch within the main flow of publishing surveillance tracks — supporting the argument that decorrelated track handling (as in EC-PO-023) may belong to a separate use case or exception path.

evidence_cards.content: When the Simulation Indicator is set in a J2 or J3 message, all data associated with that track are simulated and should not be associated with a live track.

source_locations.location: paragraph under section 4.4.2.3 SIMULATED TRACKS, sentence beginning 'When the Simulation Indicator is set...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Reinforces that simulated tracks are treated as fundamentally distinct from live tracks and must not be correlated — further evidence that decorrelation logic (including initiating new track reports with No Statement indicators) is likely outside the scope of the standard 'Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks' use case.

evidence_cards.content: Prior coordination with all interface participants is required when transmitting simulated tracks on the interface to insure that simulated tracks are not assigned TNs from other systems' TN blocks.

source_locations.location: paragraph under section 4.4.2.3 SIMULATED TRACKS, sentence beginning 'Prior coordination with all interface participants...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that simulated track handling requires special procedural safeguards, suggesting that their publication and correlation rules are governed by separate constraints — reinforcing that decorrelation behaviors like those in EC-PO-023 are not part of the canonical success scenario of this use case.

evidence_cards.content: Common tracking is defined as sharing of a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that decorrelation (breaking shared track) results in separate local tracks, supporting EC-PO-023’s claim about initiating new track reports with new numbers after decorrelation — this is part of the broader tracking protocol but not necessarily within the 'Publish' use case main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A track for which positional data has been locally derived by a C² JU but is currently being reported by another C² JU is referred to as a 'common local track', and a track for which positional data has been locally derived and is not currently being reported by another C² JU is referred to only as a 'local track'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines states resulting from decorrelation — if a C² JU decorrelates from a remote-reported track, it becomes a 'local track' under its own reporting, aligning with EC-PO-023’s postcondition of initiating a new surveillance track report with locally held data and a new track number.

evidence_cards.content: In order for common tracking to function properly, all C² JUs shall perform correlation and decorrelation of their local track data with respect to the remote data which they are receiving.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes decorrelation as a required capability for C² JUs engaged in common tracking, implying it is an integral part of the tracking lifecycle — however, does not specify whether decorrelation-triggered publication belongs in the same use case or a separate one.

evidence_cards.content: Failure to properly correlate can result in a dual designation. The protocols in this section are to be followed in order to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that decorrelation is a corrective action to resolve dual designations — suggests decorrelation may be triggered during or after publishing, but doesn’t confirm whether the resulting state (new track report) is part of the Publish use case’s postconditions or a separate process.

evidence_cards.content: Each C² JU which has a capability to originate and report real-time air, surface (maritime), land (ground), or space tracks shall have a capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria which follow.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms that decorrelation is a mandated capability tied to track origination/reporting — supports inclusion of decorrelation outcomes in postconditions of publishing, since publishing requires prior correlation/decorrelation readiness.

evidence_cards.content: The rules for correlation of land and space tracks are to be determined.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Implies that decorrelation rules for air/surface are already defined and applicable — reinforces that decorrelation behavior for air/surface tracks (as referenced in EC-PO-023) is governed by existing rules within this document, likely adjacent to publishing logic.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface, in order to prevent or eliminate dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the trigger for correlation/decorrelation — if comparison fails (i.e., no match), decorrelation occurs, leading to initiation of a new local track — directly supports EC-PO-023’s claim about post-decorrelation state including new track report with No Statement fields.

evidence_cards.content: All C² JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Mandates automatic correlation as prerequisite for track origination — implies decorrelation is also automated and thus part of the standard track management workflow, potentially embedded within the Publish use case’s alternative flows rather than a separate use case.

evidence_cards.content: In the decorrelation alternative flow (diverging from main-flow Step 6), if position or other data in a PPLI meet decorrelation criteria, the C2 JU initiates a surveillance track report using locally held data with a new track number, and reports the PPLI Track Number, Identity Indicator, and IFF/SIF Indicator fields as No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides specific postcondition details for the decorrelation variant of the use case, confirming that initiating a new track report with 'No Statement' indicators is part of this use case's successful alternative flow rather than a separate process.

evidence_cards.content: After it has been determined that a common local track satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the decorrelation shall be executed by automatically testing the local track once for correlation against remote tracks; if the test fails, a new TN (TN B) is assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the execution logic and resulting state change (assignment of new TN) for decorrelation, supporting the definition of the system state after the alternative flow completes.

evidence_cards.content: Differences in position, velocity, or altitude/elevation recognized by a JU are not resolved through conflict processing and shall not generate a J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the post-condition for the 'Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks' use case regarding surveillance data differences: the system remains in a state where these specific differences are unresolved and no termination message is generated, distinguishing this from other types of conflicts that would trigger a resolution flow.

evidence_cards.content: However, differences in these elements may cause a JU to assume that one TN represents two different tracks or different TNs are being used to report the same track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the resulting system state (post-condition) when surveillance data differences persist: the potential creation of duplicate tracks or confusion over Track Numbers, which serves as a boundary condition for the successful publication of a single consistent track.
